ceiling_statement: Relative to a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order and a fixed authority-chain semantics, the maximum attainable by any H1-H8 system is: SOUND AND COMPLETE PROOF-CARRYING RESOLUTION OVER L(G) — every string in L(G) occurring in served text is parsed by a total, coverage-gated recognizer and resolved to exactly one committed authority record carrying a verified receipt (signature chain valid to a pinned owner key, delegation valid at the receipt's genTime, revocation checked, bitemporal validity interval covering the citation's reference time), and every citation-like string outside L(G) is emitted as typed UNKNOWN-CITATION that never upgrades to a pass (H2). Beyond this ceiling lie two things NO feasible system can deliver: recognition of arbitrary natural-language reference intent outside G, and verification that the cited authority semantically supports the citing proposition — both are excluded, and any claim to deliver them without human adjudication is structurally dishonest under H1.
derivation: Computability limit: the set of natural-language strings that 'function as a citation' has no decidable characterization — surface forms are open-ended and reference intent is a semantic property of text, so by a Rice-style argument no algorithm decides it for arbitrary input; any total mechanical recognizer necessarily fixes a formal language, hence the ceiling can only be stated relative to a declared decidable G. H1 closes the only escape route: a statistical model approximating NL intent is exactly what the invariant bans from the trusted path, so its output can at most be an untrusted CANDIDATE that must re-enter through the G-verifier — it cannot raise the trusted ceiling above L(G). Within L(G), verification theory gives the exact maximum: a citation is validated when it is bound to an authority record whose authenticity chain is checkable offline with zero producer trust (H8) — signature verification against a pinned root, delegation window containment, revocation absence, and bitemporal validity are each decidable predicates over committed data, and their conjunction is the strongest offline-checkable statement about a citation's TARGET; nothing stronger exists because authority-ness beyond the committed chain (e.g. 'this court's PDF is genuine') reduces to the AX-04 origin ceiling. The semantic-support question (does the authority actually stand for the proposition?) requires an oracle for legal meaning; no formal semantics of open-textured law that is both sound and complete exists today, so under H2 the only honest output for it is UNKNOWN. Consistency: the JWS layer proves internal consistency, not authenticity — authenticity enters only through the pinned-owner chain, which is why the ceiling names the chain, not the timestamp.
relativity_note: Relative to: (1) a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order (for B0: Greek FEK/ELI references — the executable grammar to be seated where source/citation-authority.lisp and source/legal-references.lisp now hold regexes); (2) the TUF-style delegation semantics of authority-v2/roles/ROLES-MODEL.sexp with Ed25519 owner-pinning as implemented in source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp; (3) the bitemporal validity semantics of source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp (valid-time × transaction-time, genTime floor). Change any of the three and the ceiling statement changes with it.
attainment_mechanism: Every component needed is already seated in B0 — what is missing is the proof-carrying LINK, not new technology. Build: (1) a total citation recognizer as a load-time coverage-gated FSM in the exact pattern of systems/orchestrator-engine-sbcl/adapters/raw-text-adapter.lisp (which already proves at load that every state×input pair is covered), generated from an explicit grammar S-expression, seated to replace the regex layer in source/citation-authority.lisp — the article-number bound derived from corpus config instead of the hardcoded (<= num 120) at citation-authority.lisp:224; (2) each parsed reference resolves through the EXISTING verifier chain: source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp (Ed25519 owner-pin, delegation-valid-at-genTime, revocation) down to a source/legal-authority-receipt.lisp bitemporal receipt whose journal-prefix replay is already exact-sequence; the resolution emits a per-citation certificate {citation-span-hash, grammar-production-id, receipt-id, validity-interval} appended as leaves into source/merkle-authority.lisp so citation validation becomes offline recompute-and-compare (H8); (3) any citation-like string the FSM rejects becomes a typed UNKNOWN-CITATION condition routed to the source/anomaly-detection.lisp queue and BLOCKS the artifact from the top authority tier (H3) instead of being silently dropped; (4) discharge full RFC-3161 TSA chain verification with the existing strict-DER seat source/asn1-der.lisp; (5) PageRank/salience in citation-authority.lisp is demoted explicitly to untrusted advisory ranking — it is relevance, not validity, and must never gate admission.
b0_gap: B0's authority CHAIN is already proof-carrying (authority-proof-bundle.lisp owner-pin/delegation/revocation; temporal-proof.lisp JWS; ROLES-MODEL.sexp), but the citation RESOLUTION layer is heuristic-in-loop per the B0 map AX-05 row: regex extraction with the hardcoded ≤120 article cap (verified at source/citation-authority.lisp:224), cross-law citations unresolved, PageRank salience (pagerank at citation-authority.lisp:408) mixed into the same seat as validity, JWS proving consistency rather than authenticity, RFC-3161 TSA chain verification undischarged, and two quarantined dead stubs (systems/orchestrator-ai-core/citation-strategy.lisp returning constant 1.0; source/ai-citation-strategy.lisp outbound SEO tracking) contributing nothing. No per-citation certificate binds a cited reference to a verified receipt today — that link is the entire gap.
lean_obligation: Fix G as an inductive grammar with decidable membership `decG : ∀ s : String, Decidable (s ∈ L G)`, receipts `R` with `chainValid : R → Prop` (signature to pinned root, delegation window, non-revoked — each a decidable predicate over committed bytes) and `validAt : R → Time → Prop` (bitemporal containment). Let `resolve : {s // s ∈ L G} → Option R` be the system's pure resolver and `out : String → Result` its total output function. Prove: (SOUND) `∀ s h r, out s = .cited r → s ∈ L G ∧ resolve ⟨s,h⟩ = some r ∧ chainValid r ∧ validAt r (refTime s)`; (COMPLETE-rel-G) `∀ s, s ∈ L G → out s ≠ .dropped` (every grammar hit is either a verified receipt or a typed failure, never silent); (HONEST) `∀ s, s ∉ L G → out s = .unknown`, and `.unknown` is not equal to and never coerces to `.cited _` (H2 as a type-level impossibility); (CEILING) any output function satisfying H1/H5/H8 that claims `.cited r` on some s ∉ L G contradicts decidability-of-trusted-path — i.e. the trusted validated set is at most `{s | s ∈ L G ∧ chainValid (resolve s)}`.
